summary: Crenshaw County, AL former lookout site registered in 2019; a water tank stands on the site and the register says no trace of the tower remains.

facts.status_note: Register says a water tank is on the site of the former tower and no trace of the tower remains

events.note: Registered September 18, 2019 on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register; nominated by Andrew Zerbe

evidence.supports: administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
water tank on the site of the former tower
evidence.quote: Water tank is on the site of the former tower.

evidence.supports: aircraft as the most common explanation for decline; planes covered a broader area than a 100-foot tower
evidence.quote: The most common explanation is that aircraft was more efficient in spotting fires in a much broader area than a 100-foot tower could provide.

evidence.supports: neglect and climbing liability led to dismantling of these structures

evidence.quote: Today, Alabama retains only about a third of the lookouts it once had.

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: Only the Former Fire Lookout Sites page describes this site. The Kaufmann column (source 2) is general context about Alabama towers, not about this site, and the story says so. Two web searches gave no tower-specific history, so no build date, design, staffing or fire record is written. Access is not established by any source. The NHLR URL guessed at nhlr.org/lookouts/us/al/leon-fire-tower-site/ returned 404 in the crawl cache; that does not prove the site is absent from NHLR.
